programme.displayName: Terraform State and Remote Backend Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Migrate, lock, inspect, refresh, isolate and import Terraform state safely on AWS.
programme.description: Start with no lab infrastructure. Create dedicated training access, build a local-state configuration, migrate it to a private versioned S3 backend with native locking, inspect drift, use workspaces, import an existing resource and remove everything in the correct order.
programme.learningOutcome: Safely manage Terraform state throughout its lifecycle and explain the state, backend, locking, refresh-only, workspace and import concepts tested by Terraform Associate.

tasks.title: Create dedicated Terraform state training access
tasks.feature: IAM user, policy, AWS CLI profile and working folder
tasks.goal: Start with no lab infrastructure, create one temporary training identity, verify the AWS account and prepare an empty folder.
tasks.whyItMatters: State operations can change or forget infrastructure, so the learner must confirm identity, Region and folder boundaries before running Terraform.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training policy and user
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to the training AWS account as an administrator; never use the root user for this lab.

instructions.text: Sign in to the training AWS account as an administrator; never use the root user for this lab.
Open the account menu, copy the 12-digit account ID and record it as [ACCOUNT_ID].
Use the Region selector to choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Open IAM, choose Policies, then choose Create policy.
Choose JSON and paste the supplied fa-terraform-state-training-policy document.
Replace every <ACCOUNT_ID> placeholder with the recorded 12-digit account ID.
Choose Next, name the policy fa-terraform-state-training-policy, review the named S3 and Parameter Store boundaries, then choose Create policy.
Open IAM Users, choose Create user and enter fa-terraform-state-user.
Attach fa-terraform-state-training-policy directly to this temporary user.
Open the new user, choose Security credentials and create one CLI access key only if using local PowerShell or WSL.
Store the access key only in the protected AWS CLI prompt; never paste it into Terraform files, Author, Git or chat.
If using AWS CloudShell, switch to an authorized non-root training role or user before continuing.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The temporary user and narrowly named training policy exist, and the learner is not using root.
consoleSteps.warning: The policy is for this disposable training lab. An administrator must review it before attachment.

consoleSteps.title: Create and enter the working folder
consoleSteps.instruction: Open AWS CloudShell or Windows PowerShell.

instructions.text: Open AWS CloudShell or Windows PowerShell.
CloudShell: run mkdir -p ~/fa-terraform-state to create the folder even if it already exists.
CloudShell: run cd ~/fa-terraform-state to enter the folder.
CloudShell: run pwd and confirm the path ends with /fa-terraform-state.
PowerShell: run New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-state" -Force.
PowerShell: run Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\fa-terraform-state".
PowerShell: run Get-Location and confirm the path ends with fa-terraform-state.
Run terraform version and record the installed version. Terraform 1.10 or newer is required for native S3 lockfiles.
Run Get-ChildItem in PowerShell or ls -la in CloudShell and confirm the folder contains no old state or configuration.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The terminal is in one empty fa-terraform-state folder and Terraform 1.10 or newer is available.

cliSteps.explanation: Enter the temporary access key, secret, eu-west-2 and json directly into the protected prompt.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The named profile is stored locally; secrets are not printed.

cliSteps.explanation: Verify the exact caller and account before Terraform can make changes.
Verify a Terraform version that supports native S3 lockfiles.

consoleSteps.instruction: Remain inside the empty fa-terraform-state folder.

instructions.text: Remain inside the empty fa-terraform-state folder.
Create versions.tf and paste the supplied versions.tf block exactly.
Create variables.tf and paste the supplied variables.tf block exactly.
Create main.tf and paste the supplied main.tf block exactly.
Create outputs.tf and paste the supplied outputs.tf block exactly.

tasks.title: Create the protected S3 backend bucket
tasks.goal: Create one private encrypted versioned bucket outside Terraform so it can hold Terraform state.
tasks.whyItMatters: A backend must exist before Terraform can initialize it, and versioning helps recover from accidental state changes.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Create and verify the backend bucket
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Amazon S3 in the same [ACCOUNT_ID].

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 in the same [ACCOUNT_ID].
Choose Create bucket.
For Bucket name, enter fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> after replacing <ACCOUNT_ID> with the recorded 12-digit value.
For AWS Region, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Keep Object Ownership set to ACLs disabled.
Keep Block all public access selected and do not add a public bucket policy.
Turn Bucket Versioning on.
Keep default encryption enabled with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Add tag Lab = fa-terraform-state.
Choose Create bucket.
Open the exact bucket, choose Properties and verify Versioning is Enabled and Default encryption is SSE-S3.
Choose Permissions and verify all four Block Public Access settings are On.
Confirm the Objects tab is empty before state migration.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The exact fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> bucket is empty, private, encrypted and versioned.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not place ordinary files or credentials in the state bucket.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-terraform-state
cliSteps.explanation: Create the uniquely named London Region backend bucket.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response returns the bucket location.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled --profile fa-terraform-state
cliSteps.explanation: Enable recoverable object versions.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without an error.

cliSteps.explanation: Explicitly enable all bucket-level public access blocks.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without an error.

cliSteps.explanation: Explicitly configure SSE-S3 default encryption.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without an error.

cliSteps.explanation: Read the versioning setting.
Read all four public-access settings.
Read the encryption rule.

verification.title: Verify all backend protections
verification.instruction: Confirm the exact bucket name, eu-west-2 Region, Enabled versioning, SSE-S3 encryption and all four public access blocks.
verification.expectedResult: Every protection is visible and the bucket contains no objects before migration.

tasks.title: Migrate local state and enable native locking
tasks.feature: S3 backend, terraform init -migrate-state and use_lockfile
tasks.goal: Move the existing state into S3 without recreating the Parameter Store resource and enable native S3 state locking.
tasks.whyItMatters: Teams need shared state and locking so two writers cannot silently update the same state at once.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Configure and migrate the backend
consoleSteps.instruction: Create backend.tf in fa-terraform-state and paste the supplied empty S3 backend block.

instructions.text: Create backend.tf in fa-terraform-state and paste the supplied empty S3 backend block.
Create backend.hcl and paste the supplied partial backend settings.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> in backend.hcl with the recorded 12-digit account ID.
Confirm backend.hcl contains only bucket, key, Region, use_lockfile and profile settings; it must contain no access key or secret.
Run terraform fmt and terraform validate.
Run terraform init -migrate-state -backend-config=backend.hcl.
When Terraform asks whether to copy existing state to the S3 backend, read the source and destination and enter yes.
Wait for Terraform to report successful backend configuration.
Run terraform state list and confirm aws_ssm_parameter.demo is still tracked.
Run terraform plan and confirm 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
Open the S3 backend bucket and browse to terraform-state-lab/terraform.tfstate.
Verify the state object has a current version and do not download or display its contents.
Understand that use_lockfile creates a .tflock object only while Terraform holds a lock; it can disappear when the operation completes.
Run terraform plan -lock-timeout=60s and allow it to acquire and release the backend lock normally.
Refresh the S3 Objects and Versions views and identify the state key versions. Do not delete any version.

jsonBlocks.title: backend.hcl
jsonBlocks.content:
bucket       = "fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID>"
key          = "terraform-state-lab/terraform.tfstate"
region       = "eu-west-2"
use_lockfile = true
profile      = "fa-terraform-state"

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The S3 backend holds the state, the existing resource is unchanged and native lockfile support is enabled.
consoleSteps.warning: Never use -lock=false for a normal shared-state operation. Never edit state directly.

cliSteps.explanation: Format the new backend block.
Validate the configuration before changing the backend.
Copy the existing local state into the protected S3 backend after interactive confirmation.
Prove that the resource remained tracked after migration.
Confirm migration did not change infrastructure.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.

cliSteps.explanation: Use the configured backend lock and wait safely if another operation temporarily owns it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Terraform acquires the lock, completes the plan and releases it.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> --prefix terraform-state-lab/ --profile fa-terraform-state
cliSteps.explanation: List state versions without displaying state contents.
cliSteps.expectedResult: At least one terraform.tfstate version is returned.

verification.title: Verify migration without replacement
verification.instruction: Confirm terraform state list retains the parameter and terraform plan is a no-change plan.
verification.expectedResult: State migrated while the AWS resource remained intact.

verification.title: Verify remote storage
verification.instruction: Confirm the exact state key exists in the versioned S3 bucket.

tasks.title: Detect drift and use refresh-only safely
tasks.feature: Drift detection, refresh-only plans and configuration reconciliation
tasks.goal: Create one visible tag drift, review a refresh-only plan, then restore the declared configuration.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam distinguishes recording remote changes in state from changing infrastructure back to the configuration.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Create one controlled drift and reconcile it
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Systems Manager, choose Parameter Store and open /fa-terraform-state/default/demo.

instructions.text: Open Systems Manager, choose Parameter Store and open /fa-terraform-state/default/demo.
Open Tags and change only Environment from default to changed-outside-terraform.
Do not change the parameter name, type or value.
Return to fa-terraform-state and run terraform plan -refresh-only -out=refresh.tfplan.
Read the plan and confirm it records the tag difference without proposing to restore the configured value.
Run terraform show refresh.tfplan and verify only the Environment tag changed in the refresh-only plan.
Run terraform apply refresh.tfplan to record the observed remote tag in state.
Run terraform state show aws_ssm_parameter.demo and confirm state now records changed-outside-terraform.
Run terraform plan -out=reconcile.tfplan.
Confirm the normal plan proposes one in-place change restoring Environment = default from the configuration.
Run terraform apply reconcile.tfplan.
Refresh the Parameter Store Tags view and verify Environment = default.
Run terraform plan one more time and confirm no changes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner sees the difference between refresh-only state synchronization and configuration reconciliation.
consoleSteps.warning: Change only the named training parameter tag. Never experiment with unrelated production resources.

cliSteps.explanation: Create a saved plan that updates state to match the observed remote tag.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The plan shows the out-of-band Environment tag change.

cliSteps.explanation: Inspect the saved refresh-only plan.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Only the controlled tag drift is shown.

cliSteps.explanation: Record the observed remote object in state without restoring configuration yet.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Apply completes with the refreshed state.

cliSteps.explanation: Read the refreshed state.
Compare refreshed state with the unchanged HCL configuration.
cliSteps.expectedResult: One in-place update restores Environment = default.

cliSteps.explanation: Apply only the reviewed reconciliation plan.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The parameter tag returns to default.

cliSteps.explanation: Verify configuration, state and AWS agree again.
cliSteps.expectedResult: No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.

verification.title: Explain refresh-only
verification.instruction: State in one sentence what refresh-only changed and what it did not change.
verification.expectedResult: It updated Terraform state to observed AWS values; it did not restore the HCL value.

verification.title: Verify reconciliation
verification.instruction: Compare HCL, state show and the Console tag.

tasks.title: Create and remove an isolated development workspace
tasks.feature: Terraform CLI workspaces and separate backend state paths
tasks.goal: Create a development workspace, apply one isolated parameter and return safely to default.
tasks.whyItMatters: CLI workspaces create separate state instances, but they do not replace strong architectural environment separation.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Use the development workspace without changing default
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform workspace list and identify the asterisk beside default.

instructions.text: Run terraform workspace list and identify the asterisk beside default.
Run terraform workspace new development.
Run terraform workspace show and confirm development is active.
Run terraform plan -out=development.tfplan.
Confirm the plan creates /fa-terraform-state/development/demo rather than changing the default parameter.
Run terraform apply development.tfplan.
Open Parameter Store and verify both /fa-terraform-state/default/demo and /fa-terraform-state/development/demo exist.
Open the S3 bucket and identify the development workspace state under the workspace prefix without opening its contents.
Run terraform plan -destroy -out=development-destroy.tfplan and confirm only the development parameter will be destroyed.
Run terraform apply development-destroy.tfplan.
Verify the development parameter is absent while the default parameter remains.
Run terraform workspace select default.
Run terraform workspace delete development.
Run terraform workspace list and confirm only default remains.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The development state was isolated, its resource was removed, and the learner returned to default.
consoleSteps.warning: Never delete an active workspace or a workspace that still manages resources.

Create and select a separate development state instance.

Plan the development parameter with the workspace-derived name.

Prepare the development-only teardown.

Delete the empty development workspace state.

Run terraform state list and confirm both aws_ssm_parameter.demo and aws_s3_bucket.imported are tracked.

Run terraform plan -out=post-import.tfplan.
Read any proposed tag-only update, apply it if it exactly adds the declared ManagedBy and Lab tags, then run terraform plan again.
Confirm the final plan reports no changes.

tasks.title: Destroy workloads, migrate state locally and remove the backend
tasks.goal: Remove every lab resource in the only safe order and retain no credentials or state bucket.
tasks.whyItMatters: The backend must remain available until Terraform has destroyed managed resources and copied its final state elsewhere.
requiredPermissions: Use only the temporary fa-terraform-state training identity and exact named resources.

cli.reason: Complete Terraform and AWS CLI guidance is included.

consoleSteps.title: Perform the complete ordered teardown
consoleSteps.instruction: Run terraform workspace show and confirm default is active.

instructions.text: Run terraform workspace show and confirm default is active.
Run terraform state list and confirm only the default SSM parameter and imported empty S3 bucket remain.
Run terraform plan -destroy -out=destroy.tfplan.
Inspect destroy.tfplan and confirm it deletes only aws_ssm_parameter.demo and aws_s3_bucket.imported.
Run terraform apply destroy.tfplan.
Open Parameter Store and verify /fa-terraform-state/default/demo is absent.
Open S3 and verify fa-tf-import-<ACCOUNT_ID> is absent.
Run terraform state list and confirm it returns no resource addresses.
Do not delete the backend bucket yet.
Replace backend.tf with the supplied local backend block.
Run terraform init -migrate-state.
When asked to copy the final empty state from S3 to local, verify the direction and enter yes.
Run terraform state list again and confirm the migrated local state is empty.
Open fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID> in S3 and choose Empty.
Enter permanently delete and empty all object versions and delete markers in that exact bucket.
After the bucket is empty, choose Delete, enter the exact bucket name and delete it.
Open IAM as the administrator and delete the access key for fa-terraform-state-user.
Detach and delete fa-terraform-state-training-policy, then delete fa-terraform-state-user.
Delete the named fa-terraform-state AWS CLI profile from the local credentials and config files without touching other profiles.
Leave the lab folder, verify its exact path, and delete only fa-terraform-state.
Confirm no backend bucket, import bucket, training parameters, temporary IAM identity or local lab folder remains.

warnings.cost: Parameter Store standard parameters are normally free. S3 storage and requests can incur small charges. Delete every named lab resource during the final phase.
warnings.safety: Operate only on exact fa-terraform-state and fa-tf-import names. Read every plan before apply and never edit Terraform state directly.
warnings.credentials: Never paste passwords, access keys, session tokens, backend credentials, state content or plan JSON into HCL, Author, Git, screenshots or chat.
warnings.region: Use eu-west-2 for S3 and Parameter Store resources. IAM is global. Verify the AWS account before every create, import or delete operation.

steps.title: Remove the development workspace workload
steps.instruction: Destroy the development workspace parameter before returning to default and deleting the empty workspace.
steps.description: Destroy the development workspace parameter before returning to default and deleting the empty workspace.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 1 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Remove default managed resources
steps.instruction: Destroy the default Parameter Store parameter and imported empty S3 bucket using a reviewed saved destroy plan.
steps.description: Destroy the default Parameter Store parameter and imported empty S3 bucket using a reviewed saved destroy plan.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 2 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Migrate the final empty state locally
steps.instruction: Change to the local backend and run terraform init -migrate-state before touching the S3 backend bucket.
steps.description: Change to the local backend and run terraform init -migrate-state before touching the S3 backend bucket.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 3 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Empty and delete the versioned backend bucket
steps.instruction: Delete every version and delete marker only from fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID>, then delete that exact empty bucket.
steps.description: Delete every version and delete marker only from fa-tf-state-<ACCOUNT_ID>, then delete that exact empty bucket.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 4 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Remove temporary IAM access
steps.instruction: Delete the temporary access key, detach and delete the exact policy, then delete fa-terraform-state-user.
steps.description: Delete the temporary access key, detach and delete the exact policy, then delete fa-terraform-state-user.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 5 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Remove local training files
steps.instruction: Delete only the fa-terraform-state CLI profile and verified lab folder after AWS cleanup is complete.
steps.description: Delete only the fa-terraform-state CLI profile and verified lab folder after AWS cleanup is complete.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 6 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

steps.title: Acknowledge complete cleanup
steps.instruction: Confirm no named S3 bucket, SSM parameter, IAM resource, workspace, credential, plan or state file remains.
steps.description: Confirm no named S3 bucket, SSM parameter, IAM resource, workspace, credential, plan or state file remains.
steps.verification: Cleanup item 7 is visibly complete for only the exact lab targets.

findings.message: An administrator must review the exact temporary training policy and replace account placeholders before attachment.
State and plan files can contain sensitive values and must never be displayed, committed or copied into Author.
Managed resources and final state migration must complete before the versioned backend bucket is emptied and deleted.

identityBinding.rule: The local Author import must bind the currently signed-in Author and create exactly one private draft.
